@pcbeingused333 is attempting to deploy a commit to the **Guardrails AI** Team on [Vercel](https://vercel.com).

A member of the Team first needs to [authorize it](https://vercel.com/git/authorize?team=Guardrails%20AI&slug=guardrails-ai&teamId=team_acqtAxKiy6qvutCKZ3ixQRiU&type=github&job=%7B%22headInfo%22%3A%7B%22sha%22%3A%22f6a9ae2101f5d93d04568d6d906da1d286231ad2%22%7D%2C%22id%22%3A%22QmchByQXuwVeVcSZtpqkpUQuvU8VLJ4hic47bSA6E7QrGq%22%2C%22org%22%3A%22guardrails-ai%22%2C%22prId%22%3A1653%2C%22repo%22%3A%22guardrails%22%7D).

The `CI` and `Dependency Audit` workflows are showing `action_required` (fork gate) — could a maintainer press "Approve and run workflows"?

Local verification so the approval isn't a leap of faith:

- `pytest tests/unit_tests/test_merge.py -q` — 8 passed (2 new, both fail with the exact `IndexError` from the description when `merge.py` is reverted).
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on the touched files — clean.
- `pyright guardrails/merge.py` (inside the project venv, per `make type`) — 0 errors.
- Fuzzed 300,000 random `(base, source, target)` triples through `merge()` after the fix — zero crashes.
Hi, a gentle ping on this fix: the review is the only thing blocking it (the Vercel check just needs a team member to authorize the deploy). Happy to rework it if you'd prefer a different approach.
